description: Verify that DUT accepts an IPv4 datagram of up to 576 octets and replies without truncating the Data section — 576 is the minimum maximum reassembly size every conformant host must support (RFC 791 §3.1 MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
RFC 791 fixes 576 octets as the floor for MTU/reassembly support. A 576-octet Echo Request must be accepted, reassembled (or received whole), and the full payload echoed back in the Reply.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ICMP Echo Request, total IPv4 size = 576 octets, with a known data pattern

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: Echo Reply
      - data field present in full (no truncation)
      - data bytes match the Request's   ← key check

[Pass condition]
Reply payload matches the Request's payload, full length.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_payload_truncated — Reply was emitted but the data section was shorter than the Request's
• Fail_payload_mismatch — Reply emitted at full length but data bytes differed
• Fail_timeout — DUT did not emit a Reply within the window

verdicts.Pass: Reply carried the full 576-byte echo — normal
verdicts.Fail_payload_truncated: Reply data section truncated — DUT could not handle 576 bytes
verdicts.Fail_payload_mismatch: Reply data differed from Request — corruption in echo path
verdicts.Fail_timeout: DUT did not emit a Reply within the window
